messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — we're planning to remove the X-Redwood-Signer v1 fallback from SDK auth checks on 2026-04-12. This will be a breaking change for older partner SDKs that still rely on the legacy header. Need a short plan for marketplace bundles + SI rollouts. Who needs to be looped in?
ana: tagging @liz (marketplace) and @jiho (SDK). Can you confirm surface area? Are partner CLI packages or marketplace installer images affected?
j i h o: FYI this change touches the server auth layer and SDK client negotiation logic. Old clients send `X-Redwood-Signer: v1` and servers accepted it. New default will be `X-Redwood-Signer: v2` only. Quick diff: we will drop the fallback branch in the gateway auth middleware.
jiho: code snippet of the compatibility check we plan to remove:
```js
// current (will be removed)
if (req.headers['x-redwood-signer'] === 'v2' || req.headers['x-redwood-signer'] === 'v1') {
  accept();
}

// new (post-change)
if (req.headers['x-redwood-signer'] === 'v2') accept();
```
sam: We should not flip this without a graceful runway. Recommend: 3-week deprecation window, canary for 48h in us-west-2, and gateway feature-flag to re-enable fallback if high error spike.
liz: Marketplace concern: some vendor bundles pin older SDKs; if we break them they'll get booted by automated health checks. We need a packaging bump or compatibility shim in the marketplace image. Also add a marketplace warning banner for affected listings.
ana: Proposed timeline:
- Week 0: announce to partners + vendor slack list, post deprecation notice in vendor portal
- Week 1: roll canary to 10% traffic in staging and one small SI partner (opt-in)
- Week 2: expand canary, publish SDK patch and marketplace image with bump and migration notes
- Week 3: flip in prod, monitor, and keep gateway feature-flag for 72h fallback if needed
Can @maria or @sam own the canary runbook?
maria: I can own partner comms + vendor list. @sam please own the canary runbook and rollback play. I'll prepare partner email and marketplace banner copy.
jiho: SDK migration notes draft (short):
- If you see 401 after 2026-04-12, update SDK to >= v2.3.0 which sets `X-Redwood-Signer: v2`.
- Temporary workaround (not recommended): add header `X-Redwood-Signer: v2` in your client until package is updated.
- Example curl: `curl -H "X-Redwood-Signer: v2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate`

jiho: Also adding an npm deprecation notice on older package versions. We'll tag a semver-major compliance note.
liz: For marketplace listing owners: we can schedule an automated compatibility scan next week and flag affected images. Will also generate a 'compatibility advisory' SKU note.
sam: Canary runbook checklist (short):
- deploy gateway feature-flag to canary cluster
- route 10% of traffic for 48h, check 5xx/401 rates
- smoke test with sample partner workloads (list: SI-A, SI-C)
- if >2x baseline 401s, rollback flag and notify partners
- escalate to eng-oncall if rollback fails

nana: Partner comms draft: "Heads up — auth header v1 fallback removal on Apr 12. Please update SDKs or add header override. See migration guide: <internal link>" Should we include a compatibility grace period window?
maria: Yes include 3-week grace window and links to SDK binaries + marketplace patched images. I'll also open a shared spreadsheet for partner statuses.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway-feature-flag canary -> 2026-04-01T22:00Z (initiated by sam).
jiho: small ask — can CI publish a compatibility badge for marketplace images after they pass the scan? that will help SIs.
liz: yes we can show a green "compat v2" badge on listings that pass the scan. I'll coordinate with growth to display it.
maria: OK — action items: @sam run canary, @jiho publish SDK patch + npm deprecation, @liz run compatibility scans + badge, @ana own partner outreach list. I'll send the partner email today. :thumbsup:
